ai.title: Remove FLUSHFAILED event from analytics flush error handler
ai.summary: The catch block in flushAnalytics now swallows errors silently, removing the trackEvent(AnalyticsEvent.FLUSH_FAILED) call. This prevents recursive event tracking when the flush itself fails. Scope limited to common/src/analytics.ts.

eli5.text: When the app tries to save your usage stats in the background and something goes wrong, it used to send yet another tracking message about that failure. That second message could sometimes trigger another failure, creating a loop, so the app now simply ignores any error while saving and stays quiet about it. You won't see any visible difference, but the app is less likely to get stuck or send confusing extra reports when it has a hiccup saving your data.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.288
ai.summary: Bumped npm-app/package.json version from 1.0.287 to 1.0.288. No functional code changes included in this commit.

eli5.text: Your AI coding helper can now search and replace text in much larger files than before, files up to 64,000 tokens instead of only 16,000, so edits inside big documents are less likely to fail or cut off. While doing that, it also switched to a different, more efficient model for handling those large-file edits. This update went live on May 22, 2025, and applies to anyone using the tool today.

ai.title: Make readline public in CLI to fix client circular dependency
ai.summary: Promoted `rl` from private to public in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` to allow direct access from `npm-app/src/client.ts`. This eliminates the need to pass the `readline.Interface` via `ClientOptions` and removes the circular dependency risk by importing `CLI` directly in the client. The `Client` class now accesses `CLI.getInstance().rl` for login event listeners, simplifying the constructor signature.

eli5.text: The internal login system that connects your computer to the developer tool was reorganized so two parts can talk to each other directly. Previously, one component had to receive a piece of information through a shared settings package every time it needed to ask the other component a question, which created a fragile circular connection. Now the component that manages your typing and responses shares that piece of information directly with the login helper, so the login helper no longer needs to wait for it to be passed in. This makes the login process more reliable and prevents the two parts from accidentally blocking each other.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.289
ai.summary: Version string in npm-app/package.json incremented from 1.0.288 to 1.0.289. Internal release metadata update.

eli5.text: Today's update makes the assistant's chat window accessible to more parts of the app, which fixes a connection problem some people were hitting where the assistant couldn't talk to itself properly. You won't see anything new on screen, but things that were stuck should now load correctly. This fix is live now for everyone using the current version.

ai.title: codesearch pattern JSON stringify
ai.summary: Updated `handleCodeSearch` in `npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts` to use `JSON.stringify` for the search pattern instead of stripping quotes. The command construction now embeds the JSON string directly, adjusting the trailing dot syntax. This ensures patterns containing quotes are preserved and correctly escaped for the underlying `rg` execution.

eli5.text: When you search your code, the system now keeps your search words exactly as you type them, even if they include quotation marks. Previously, it quietly removed all quotes from your search before looking, which made some searches miss the right results. This only affects internal searches within the tool, so you won't notice any difference unless your search term contains quotes. This fix is active now.

ai.title: Version 1.0.290
ai.summary: npm-app/package.json version bumped to 1.0.290. Internal release marker.

eli5.text: The AI assistant you use has been updated to a new version that packages together a behind-the-scenes improvement to how it searches for code patterns. This update, now live, lets the assistant better handle complex search terms by converting them into a more precise format when looking up code. If you noticed the assistant occasionally misunderstanding or missing the mark on nuanced code searches, this version should handle those requests more reliably. No visible changes to the interface will be obvious, but the assistant’s internal search tool now performs a small but meaningful step to keep its queries clean and accurate.
